feature: UI "hello world" — proves a headless build agent can trigger + read back a real UI test result end to end
notes: Part of Epic #803, UI sibling of #957's hello-world-sql.json. Purpose is NOT to test deep
product logic — it proves the #898 remote-trigger-over-HTTP pipeline (headless POST
/admin/deploy/test-run -> BuildConsole claims + runs the manifest via a live WebView2 ->
POST .../complete -> headless GET .../<runId> poll) can drive a real browser and read back a
genuine pass/fail, so more complex manifests can be trusted.
CONTENT ASSERTION REDESIGN (#1027) — the hero headline is now a FULLY RANDOMIZED runtime set, not
a small static one. /api/public/hero-headlines returns every active admin-authored headline (the
seed migration shipped 3, but the live table is now ~50, all editable at runtime via the admin
Hero Headlines screen). useHeroHeadlines.ts SHUFFLES that whole set on the client (Fisher–Yates)
and types each headline out ONE CHARACTER AT A TIME into the <h1 data-testid="hero-headline">
(leadText + gradientText). So at the instant an `expect` step samples the DOM, the element shows a
PARTIAL (in-progress) slice of a RANDOM entry — almost never a full, specific, predictable string.
Why the OLD approach was wrong: this manifest used to (a) extract only $[0].leadText into
{{heroLeadText}} and (b) assert the DOM via a FIXED any-of list of {{heroLeadText}} plus the 3
seed lead_texts, using #1016's `textContains` (rendered text CONTAINS one of the phrases). Both
halves assumed a tiny static set AND fully-typed text. Against a shuffled 50-entry set that is
false: the shown headline is usually NOT $[0] and NOT one of the 3 seeds, and even when it is, the
`contains` direction only holds AFTER the whole leadText has finished typing — a partial slice
fails it. The result was a check that would spuriously fail most real runs, or (with the old fixed
list) silently only ever pass on the rare shuffle+timing coincidence. It never actually verified
the general case.
The new design captures the REAL set and matches structurally, no hardcoded copy:
(1) ENDPOINT + FULL-SET CAPTURE — the top-level apiTests GET (HttpTestExecutor's proven HttpClient
path, no browser) asserts status 200, $[0].leadText exists, and containsNone the usual junk
sentinels (scoped to the $[0].leadText string field, so a legitimate seasonalLabel:null elsewhere
can't false-fail 'null'). Its `extract` now uses a NEW `[*]` array wildcard — jsonPath
"$[*].leadText" collects EVERY headline's leadText (the whole real set, whatever its size) into
{{heroLeads}}, stored as a SetDelimiter-joined blob (#1027, TestRunVariables.SetDelimiter, U+001F —
a control char that never appears in real copy). This replaces the single-node $[0].leadText
extract entirely.
(2) DOM-INTEGRATION — step 3's `expect` uses the NEW #1027 `textPrefixOfAny` field against
["{{heroLeads}}"]. The executor fans that one {{name}} out into the full candidate set (SplitSet)
and passes when the element's REAL rendered text (el.innerText/textContent) is PREFIX-RELATED to at
least one real entry: the shorter of (rendered, entry) is a prefix of the longer, case-insensitive.
That holds while an entry is mid-type (rendered is a prefix of entry) AND once typing runs past the
leadText into the gradient tail (entry is a prefix of rendered) — i.e. at essentially every non-empty
instant of the animation, for WHICHEVER headline the shuffle happened to pick. This is what ties
'the API served this real set' to 'the DOM genuinely displays a member of it', without depending on
the nondeterministic shuffle order or on a full-typed snapshot. Empty rendered text never matches
(an empty <h1> is not a genuine headline). It composes with #1024's expect-step polling: the poll
re-checks every ~250ms across the timeoutMs window and passes the moment the relationship holds.
This is real new framework capability, not a one-off manifest fix: `[*]`-wildcard extract
(TestRunVariables) and the `textPrefixOfAny` expect matcher (UiTestExecutor) are reusable by any
future manifest asserting on randomized or progressively-rendered content.
The hero <h1> (data-testid="hero-headline") is the rotation element specifically — separate from the
inline home quiz's data-testid="quiz-result" — so it always shows a headline regardless of any prior
quiz interaction. Step 2 keeps the header CTA button (data-testid="get-real-score-cta", a stable
code-literal element, not DB content) visible check as the structural 'did it load' half of the proof.
If the whole headline table is ever emptied, {{heroLeads}} would be empty and the extract fails loudly
at its source (jsonPath matched no elements) rather than the DOM step failing mysteriously later.
